# Pinned TZif transition vectors

The four TZif blobs are byte-for-byte public-domain tz database files from Jiff revision `fff640d47f72ca6d3a122678315bbd76488306fe`, `crates/jiff/src/tz/testdata/`. Their hashes and the Jiff oracle's source/binary/lockfile identities are in `vectors.json`. Jiff's code and test-vector attribution is in `third-party/NOTICES.md` (MIT).

Jiff 0.2.38 with only the `std` feature supplies independent expected results. No ambient tzdb, clock, locale or host zone participates. Seed `2026102505` identifies a deterministic bounded generator, not statistical coverage. The permanent data includes upstream golden endpoints from `crates/jiff/src/tz/timezone.rs:2663-2700`, Sitka's whole-day fold at `:2770-2802,3191-3220`, and the three Earlier examples from `ambiguous.rs:517-537`. Before generation, the independent oracle was checked against their fixed goldens (30 timezone vectors plus the three Earlier examples).

160 rows, at most ten per runtime partition. Each of four upstream zones has two selected transitions. Five additional rows use the 65-byte minimized negative-fraction regression with one offset-changing transition; these are justified controls for the reproduced boundary discrepancy. New York/Dublin/Tasmania use both 2024 transitions; Sitka uses its 1867 odd-offset whole-day fold and a 2050 transition determined by its POSIX footer. Exact transitions and both civil endpoints have ±1 ns and ±1 second neighborhoods. Each civil row evaluates all three disambiguations. Fixed UTC, negative Unix times, epoch, year bounds, Gregorian leap/month validity, TimeOfDay leap-second rejection, malformed magic and truncation complete the matrix.

Each row retains the oracle's raw result, an exact expected-output projection, input and output SHA256, origin and disposition. Civil values and expected fields/timestamps enter the runtime as host-built literals; no Hirsel parser manufactures expectations. The harness embeds the same hashed TZif bytes and emits a line for every row. It compares each engine directly to the independent expected bytes, return status and typed result categories. Source rejection, V rejection, checked-H trap, timeout and tooling failure fail the test. Partitions retain every selected ID; unavailable native tools cannot pass.

The applicable contracts are `docs/spec/std-library.md`, “Civil dates and times” (valid Date/TimeOfDay fields; no leap second; years -9999..9999) and “Time zones” (supplied TZif versions 1–4; first/last transition and POSIX footer; Earlier/Later/Reject). Invalid TZif errors are projected to `scalar.ParseError.Invalid`, using the paragraph beginning “time_zone.from_tzif(data) returns ... Invalid for any other malformed data: a wrong magic or truncated block”. This maps Jiff's free-text parser error to Hirsel's specified typed error, without treating unsupported upstream features as mandatory acceptance. Leap records are skipped per that same paragraph; this matrix does not import leap-aware zone files. No leap-second TimeOfDay is constructed.

Regenerate with a pinned Jiff checkout, Rust 1.99.0, default features disabled, `features=["std"]`, using `TimeZone::tzif` on these exact four files and `following` from 2024-01-01 UTC (first three zones), 1867-01-01 and 2050-01-01 UTC (Sitka), selecting two transitions per zone. Query each instant and each civil endpoint neighborhood described above. Retain raw results before projecting timestamp integers, offset seconds, civil fields and gap/fold categories. Generator scratch, executables and campaign receipts are intentionally external to the source tree.

Two adapted-domain vectors (`utc-civil-135`, `utc-civil-139`) preserve raw Jiff timestamp-overflow errors. Jiff Timestamp reserves approximately 26 hours at either DateTime edge, while Hirsel states: “time.Timestamp holds signed i128 unix_nanoseconds” (“Durations and timestamps”, first Timestamp paragraph) and “date_time.to_timestamp(dt, offset) is its inverse” (“Civil dates and times”, paragraph beginning “A fixed offset is i32 seconds east of UTC”). For these two valid civil inputs the oracle uses Jiff's independent civil `epoch.duration_until(dt).as_nanos() - offset_seconds * 1000000000`; all three policies select the sole UTC offset. The adapter never calls Hirsel. These expected values extend the permitted timestamp domain; they do not change a language rule.

Offset lookup deliberately differs from pinned Jiff at a negative fractional instant immediately before a TZif transition. The contract in “Time zones” states: “Offset lookup selects the transition in effect at the instant; negative non-integral timestamps use the floor second, deliberately differing from Jiff's truncation toward zero.” For `sitka-instant-103` and `minimal-instant-156`, raw Jiff uses the post-transition offset. The independent adapter obtains the expected offset by calling Jiff on `Timestamp::from_second(ns.div_euclid(1000000000))`, then calls that Jiff Offset's `to_datetime` on the original timestamp to preserve its nanoseconds. It never calls Hirsel or copies Hirsel's result. The two records retain raw outputs and the `negative-fraction-floor` disposition. No production algorithm is changed.
